name: postgres-millions
title: PostgreSQL millions — durable sessions, a few hot
summary: Millions of session actors in PostgreSQL, almost all idle with a pending timeout, a few thousand hot: the population grows under traffic while hot events, cold events and run() stay as cheap as with a thousand.
description: Runs on the PostgreSQL instance of the PostgreSQL binding, in a database of its own (tinyactors_millions; durable: the population is kept between runs, about 600 bytes per actor — --param reset=1 starts over). Every actor is a session: a small set of ids and a timeout a day after its last touch, so each idle actor has a pending timer. Four pgbench spawners grow the population to 2,000,000 (--param population) while the traffic runs; then they stop. The traffic is what an application would run: 6 clients touching a hot set of 10,000 actors (--param hot), 2 clients touching random actors anywhere in the population, and a scheduler calling tinyactors.run() five times a second. The bench measures every second with cheap queries only and probes one hot event, one cold event and one run(): with millions stored, run() finds work through indexes, an event costs one row, and memory per backend stays flat. Mutations: a flash crowd (ten times the hot set), a cold sweep, one very hot actor (8 clients on one row lock), a database restart.

flash-crowd.title: Flash crowd (20 s)
flash-crowd.description: 4 more clients over ten times the hot set: rows that were cold become hot

cold-sweep.title: Cold sweep (20 s)
cold-sweep.description: 4 clients touching random actors among all of them: no row is in cache twice

hot-actor.title: One hot actor (20 s)
hot-actor.description: 8 clients on a single actor: its row lock serializes them; the rate holds

restart.title: Restart PostgreSQL
restart.description: A fast shutdown and start: the population, its timers and the traffic come back
